verses.1: A song. A psalm for the sons of Korah.
verses.2: Great is the LORD and highly praised in the city of our God, in his holy mountain.
verses.3: Beautiful in its splendor, the joy of all the earth, is Mount Zion, the northern slopes, the city of the great king.
verses.4: God is known in its citadels as a fortress.
verses.5: For behold, the kings have gathered, they passed by together.
verses.6: They saw it and were astonished, they trembled, they were dismayed.
verses.7: Trembling seized them there, pain like a woman in labor.
verses.8: With a mighty wind, you will shatter the ships of Tarshish.
verses.9: As we have heard, so have we seen in the city of the LORD of Hosts, in the city of our God, which God will establish forever. Selah.
verses.10: We have received, O God, your steadfast love in the midst of your temple.
verses.11: According to your name, O God, so is your praise to the ends of the earth; your righteousness is full in your right hand.
verses.12: Let Mount Zion rejoice, let the daughters of Judah be glad for your judgments.
verses.13: Walk around Zion, encircle her, count her towers,
verses.14: take careful note of her ramparts, that you may tell it to the next generation:
verses.15: for this is our God forever and ever; he will be our guide to eternity.

notes:
Notes
- v. 8: "With a mighty wind, you will shatter the ships of Tarshish" — the Hebrew reads "בְּרוּחַ קָדִים תְּשַׁבֵּר אֳנִיּוֹת תַּרְשִֽׁישׁ" (literally "with a wind of the east you will break ships of Tarshish"). The reference to "ships of Tarshish" is a poetic metaphor for distant or powerful adversaries. The translation follows the literal meaning without assuming additional context.
